state.brief: Edit the supplied flat charcoal base-color swatch into the following complete material texture. Keep its square opaque canvas, replace its uniform fill with natural surface variation, and preserve the intended restrained palette. Use case: stylized-concept. Create one square, full-bleed, flat diffuse-color texture for fire-damaged metal on a stylized M1A1 wreck in a 3D strategy game. Show only the surface color, straight on with uniform flat illumination. A connected warm charcoal soot field with irregular ragged patches of heat-dulled neutral-gray substrate, varied smaller flakes and scuffs, and restrained crumbly tonal variation. The damage should feel naturally irregular and layered, with broad and medium detail that survives downsampling. Keep it suitable for a restrained low-poly game material. This is synthesized artwork, not historical evidence or a measured burn map.
constraints: Only a flat albedo source: no perspective, directional light, reflections, cast shadows, ambient-occlusion crevices, bevels, raised or curled flakes, or simulated surface depth.

Use warm charcoal around #39302b, deeper charcoal around #211f1d, muted gray around #4b4943 and restrained ash gray no brighter than approximately #76746c. No white, luminous centers or bright highlights.
Roughly two-thirds connected dark soot and one-third irregular gray material variation; distribute varied-scale features across the full image. Avoid a central composition or a few isolated stickers.
No circular or oval patches, soft radial halos, cloudy airbrush spots, parallel stripes, tiled repetition, neat boundaries or symmetrical motifs.
No intact beige paint islands: the tank's original desert paint will be preserved separately outside the burn zone.
No tank, objects, panel seams, fasteners, frames, borders, symbols, lettering or labels. Opaque background; square texture only.
Natural ragged color boundaries with a little fine breakup; avoid heavy photographic grain or decorative noise. The image will be sampled and verified through FormSeed2D before any model binding.
